🌐 Blazor WebAssembly

Run BLite directly in the browser. The BLite.Wasm package provides OPFS and IndexedDB storage backends so you can embed a full ACID-safe document database in any Blazor WASM application — no server required.

Installation

dotnet add package BLite.Wasm

BLite.Wasm targets net10.0-browser and depends on BLite. It adds two storage backends built on browser APIs and a DI extension for Blazor WASM projects.

Quick Start — Blazor WASM

Register BLite in Program.cs and inject it into any component:

Program.cs

using BLite.Wasm;

var builder = WebAssemblyHostBuilder.CreateDefault(args);

// Registers BLite with automatic backend selection (OPFS → IndexedDB fallback)
builder.Services.AddBLiteWasm("mydb");

Counter.razor

@inject BLiteEngine Db

@code {
    private async Task SaveAsync()
    {
        var col = Db.GetOrCreateCollection("events");
        col.Insert(new BsonDocument { ["ts"] = DateTime.UtcNow });
    }
}

Storage Backends

BLite.Wasm ships two storage backends. BLiteWasm.CreateAsync() automatically selects OPFS when available and falls back to IndexedDB:

BackendAPIPerformanceCompatibility
OPFSFileSystemSyncAccessHandleHigh — synchronous I/O from Worker threadsChrome 102+, Firefox 111+, Safari 15.2+
IndexedDBAsync IDB transactionsModerate — async JS interop per pageAll modern browsers
// Automatic selection (recommended)
var engine = await BLiteWasm.CreateAsync("mydb");

// Force a specific backend
var engine = await BLiteWasm.CreateAsync("mydb", WasmStorageBackend.IndexedDb);
var engine = await BLiteWasm.CreateAsync("mydb", WasmStorageBackend.Opfs);

IPageStorage Abstraction

Starting in BLite 4.3, the storage engine is decoupled from the file system via the IPageStorage and IWriteAheadLog interfaces. All existing PageFile and WriteAheadLog behaviour is unchanged; WASM backends simply plug in as alternative implementations.

// Core interface — browser backends implement this
public interface IPageStorage
{
    int PageSize { get; }
    uint NextPageId { get; }
    void Open();
    void ReadPage(uint pageId, Span<byte> destination);
    ValueTask ReadPageAsync(uint pageId, Memory<byte> destination, CancellationToken ct);
    void WritePage(uint pageId, ReadOnlySpan<byte> source);
    uint AllocatePage();
    void FreePage(uint pageId);
    void Flush();
    Task FlushAsync(CancellationToken ct);
}

In-Memory Storage

MemoryPageStorage and MemoryWriteAheadLog are also available in the base BLite package. They require no file system — useful for unit tests, ephemeral caches, and server-side preview scenarios.

// Create a fully in-memory engine — no file system required
var engine = BLiteEngine.CreateInMemory();

// With custom page size
var engine = BLiteEngine.CreateInMemory(pageSize: 8192);

// Custom storage via StorageEngine constructor
var storage = new MemoryPageStorage(pageSize: 4096);
var wal = new MemoryWriteAheadLog();
var engine = new BLiteEngine(new StorageEngine(storage, wal));

WASM Storage Classes

OpfsPageStorage

Uses FileSystemSyncAccessHandle via JS interop. Pages are stored as sequential regions in a single OPFS file. Must be called from a Worker thread (not the main browser thread). Delivers the best throughput of the two browser backends.

IndexedDbPageStorage

Uses async IndexedDB transactions via [JSImport]. Each page is stored as a keyed blob in an IDB object store. Compatible with all modern browsers including those without OPFS. Data is exchanged as base64 strings to satisfy [JSImport] async constraints.

OpfsWriteAheadLog

Appends WAL records to a dedicated OPFS .wal file. Binary format is identical to the file-based WriteAheadLog — full crash recovery is supported.

IndexedDbWriteAheadLog

Stores WAL records as serialised byte arrays in an IDB object store. TruncateAsync() clears all entries in a single IDB transaction.

DocumentDbContext in WASM

The typed DocumentDbContext API works in Blazor WASM via a new pluggable constructor that accepts a StorageEngine directly:

public class AppDb : DocumentDbContext
{
    public AppDb(StorageEngine storage) : base(storage) { }

    public DocumentCollection<Todo> Todos => GetCollection<Todo>();
}

// Blazor WASM Program.cs
builder.Services.AddSingleton(async sp =>
{
    var engine = await BLiteWasm.CreateAsync("appdb");
    return new AppDb(engine.StorageEngine);
});

Blazor WASM Counter Demo

A complete sample is available in the repository at samples/BLite.BlazorWasm. It demonstrates a counter that persists across page reloads using the OPFS backend with automatic IndexedDB fallback.

// Clone the BLite repo and run the sample
git clone https://github.com/EntglDb/BLite
cd BLite/samples/BLite.BlazorWasm
dotnet run

💡 Tip: AddBLiteWasm() automatically detects OPFS availability at runtime and falls back to IndexedDB without any configuration change. You only need to force a backend if you have specific requirements.
